sources.entry: markdown-it-py - Markdown parser with 100% CommonMark support, extensions, and syntax plugins.

summary.one_liner: A Python port of the markdown-it Markdown parser that follows the CommonMark spec and supports configurable rules and plugins.
summary.what_it_does: Parses Markdown text into tokens and renders it to HTML, following the CommonMark spec for baseline parsing. The MarkdownIt class takes a preset (such as "commonmark") and options like breaks and html, and you can enable extra syntax such as tables with enable(). Plugins are added with use(), and the README's example pairs it with front-matter and footnote plugins from the mdit-py-plugins package. Rules can be added or replaced for custom syntax. A command-line tool, markdown-it, converts files, stdin, or runs an interactive prompt, with an --enable-tables flag because tables are off by default. The README describes it as a Python port of markdown-it and its associated plugins.
use_cases: convert Markdown files to HTML in Python
add tables or footnotes to Markdown parsing
parse Markdown into tokens for custom processing
convert Markdown from the command line
parse front matter in Markdown documents
how_to_run: from markdown_it import MarkdownIt; md = MarkdownIt("commonmark"); html = md.render(text)
notable: Full CommonMark baseline with a configurable rule set that can be extended or replaced
Plugin system for syntax extensions, with a plugin list linked from the README
Command-line interface with batch, stdin, and interactive modes
README describes it as a member of Google's Assured Open Source Software
Optional markdown-it-pyrs Rust binding mentioned for more speed
caveats: Tables are disabled by default, as in CommonMark, and must be enabled explicitly
Linkify and plugin features need optional extras (linkify, plugins)
The README's security section is only linked, not described in the text provided
